title: Account Sharing Detection

description.intro:
You've compiled a list of IP addresses of all the clients connected to your service and the username associated with each one. Assume all IPs are unique and username lengths are between 1 and 30. We say a username is being shared if it appears in two connections.

If usernames are being shared, return an IP of any of them. Otherwise, return an empty string.
examples:
Example 1: connections = [("203.0.113.10", "mike"), ("298.51.100.25", "bob"),
("292.0.2.5", "mike"), ("203.0.113.15", "bob2")]
Output: "203.0.113.10". User "mike" is connected from that IP and "292.0.2.5",
so "292.0.2.5" would also be a valid output.

Example 2: connections = [("111.0.0.0", "mike"), ("111.0.0.1", "mike"),
("111.0.0.2", "bob"), ("111.0.0.3", "bob")]
Output: "111.0.0.0". Any of the IPs would be a valid output.
constraints: The length of connections is at most 10^5
Username lengths are between 1 and 30 characters
All usernames contain only lowercase letters
description.approach:
The naive solution loops over every pair of IPs in a nested loop to check for repeated usernames:

For each IP ip1
    For each IP ip2 after ip1
        Check if they have the same username
By controlling where we start the inner loop, we avoid accessing each pair twice, but the time complexity is still quadratic. This is the perfect opportunity for the linear scan tradeoff.

Instead of doing nested loops, we can use a set to keep track of usernames we've seen before. For each connection:

If we've seen this username before, return the current IP
Otherwise, add the username to the set
This improves the runtime from O(n^2) to O(n) but worsens the extra space from O(1) to O(n).

complexity:
Time & Space Analysis
n: the number of connections

Time: O(n) - we make a single pass through the connections array, and each set operation (insertion and lookup) takes O(1) time on average.

Extra space: O(n) - in the worst case, we may need to store all usernames in the set before finding a duplicate.

tests.python:
def run_tests():
  tests = [
      # Example 1 
      ([("203.0.113.10", "mike"), ("298.51.100.25", "bob"),
        ("292.0.2.5", "mike"), ("203.0.113.15", "bob2")], "203.0.113.10"),
      # Example 2 
      ([("111.0.0.0", "mike"), ("111.0.0.1", "mike"),
        ("111.0.0.2", "bob"), ("111.0.0.3", "bob")], "111.0.0.0"),
      # Example 3 
      ([("111.0.0.0", "mike"), ("111.0.0.1", "mike2"),
        ("111.0.0.2", "mike3"), ("111.0.0.3", "mike4")], ""),
      # Edge case - empty list
      ([], ""),
      # Edge case - single connection
      ([("1.1.1.1", "alice")], ""),
  ]
  for connections, want in tests:
    got = account_sharing(connections)

    # Check if got matches want directly
    if got == want:
      continue

    # If want is empty, got must also be empty
    if want == "":
      assert got == "", f"\naccount_sharing({connections}): got: {          got}, want: {want}\n"
      continue

run_tests()
